note: The law every host on every renderer answers to: a `spawn-job` effect obliges its host to START the job, STEP it until a terminal `job-step`, and answer the guest with `Event::JobCompleted` carrying that step's bytes. A host that admits the effect and never pumps it is silent breakage — on the wgpu target every `interactionSelect`/`interactionHover` published the right wire message and was never applied, because the bridge dropped the effect outright (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, `📓️wgpu-world3d-interaction-2026-09-13.md` §7).

budget.note: One host admission's static budget. `stepCeiling` is the host's patience, not the job's expected cost: a framework reserved tool job reaches `done` in two steps (`🔌️plugin/🦀️.rs`'s `drive_framework_reserved_spawn_like_host` asserts exactly that).

placements.note: The WIT `enum job-placement` vocabulary. jco lowers a WIT `enum` to a BARE string, not a `{tag}` record — measured on 6118: `placement: "isolated"` on every reserved tool job. An unknown spelling is refused, never defaulted: guessing `inline` would run a pooled job inside the spawning instance's own turn budget.

transcripts.note: The measured shape of `interactionSelect`/`interactionHover` on generation3d: one `running`, then `done` with the reserved job's output bytes.
A job whose whole body fits one slice needs no `running` at all.
A guest that refuses its own job still owes its actor an event — the parked request resolves `Err`, and the actor sees the refusal instead of hanging forever.
A driver that stops the instant it sees `done` and one that read a batch must hand over the SAME completion.
The ceiling is inclusive: 32 observations whose last one is terminal is a completion, not a stall.

refusals.note: A host that admitted the effect and never stepped it — literally the wgpu defect, expressed as a transcript.
More observations than one admission grants is a DRIVER bug and must not be laundered into a completion.

completedEvent.note: What the host sends back. The guest correlates on `job` alone — the `job` id IS the parked request id (`⚛️reactor/🔄️turn/🦀️.rs`), so no host-side request table exists. `kind` is the actor-boundary event envelope's tag; `payload` is the WIT `job-completed-event` record, and `outcome` is its `completion-result` variant.
